rules.title: Every asymmetry is named
rules.statement: A part meant to be symmetric is compared with its mirror, both ways, against a list of named exceptions. Every asymmetry has a function and a name.
rules.why: An asymmetry of 19 cm3 in 13 lumps was found by the owner on a screenshot.

attest.question: Is this part meant to be mirror-symmetric, and is every asymmetry named?
labels: compared with its mirror both ways: every difference is a named exception

rules.note: Deferred: becomes a mirror comparison of the body.

rules.title: A part is centred on its own axis
rules.statement: A structural part is centred on the axis of its own joint, never on a neighbour. An asymmetry is fixed by adding material, not by cutting. Geometry that is not used is removed, even when that makes the part asymmetric.
rules.why: A frame was centred on a fan instead of on its gearbox and took more than four iterations to correct.

rules.title: A bought or chiral part is turned, never mirrored
rules.statement: A bought or chiral part is never mirrored: the "mirrored" side is the same part turned by 180 deg. Paired parts are turned copies of one part, so that one STL serves both. A joint group is clocked only by multiples of the symmetry of its hole pattern. Identical parts are one component with several occurrences.
rules.why: An exporter option that flipped a part mirrored chiral parts; it was found before printing.

rules.title: Outlines are regular and shared
rules.statement: Outlines are regular: tangent arcs and straight lines. Two plates that lie on each other take their outline from one function.
rules.why: No lost print is on record. An outline typed twice drifts apart at the first change.
